minutes.headline: Water commissioners offered a resident a reduced high-usage bill and meter swap; borrowing and bylaw decisions deferred.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District commissioners heard a resident contest a high-usage bill and offered to recalculate it at the first block rate and swap his meter. They discussed the Hickory Hills security camera, the Mass Ave main replacement and its temporary borrowing, and approved updated rules and regulations. They objected strongly to the Planning Board's draft water protection bylaw, and public comment centered on that bylaw and PFAS treatment costs.

public_comment.topic: Contested an exceptionally high usage bill for one quarter, citing a toilet leak that was repaired, and asked about meter testing.
Relayed parents' concern that children in bathing suits at the swim beach were captured by the Hickory Hills camera and asked whether it could be turned.
Questioned the beach, golf carts and kayaks in the Zone One easement area; urged review of the easement and suggested a fence.
Said changing the camera angle would satisfy residents seeking privacy.
Criticized the draft water protection bylaw as an end run by a special interest group, urged the board to attend the Planning Board as a unified group, and asked about PFAS.
Asked about engineering proposals, urged the board to visit the Ayer PFAS plant, and said the presentation on the cost lacked detail.

votes.motion: Approve the rules and regulations of the Lunenburg Water District as written

budget_items.what_was_said: The board offered to charge the first block rate for the whole usage instead of the higher tiers, and to waive finance charges. The superintendent will calculate the amount and call the resident.
A fee applies to test a meter and is not charged if the meter is found faulty.
Grant funded the lead service line inventory and GIS mapping; the system was reported lead free.

budget_items.topic: Temporary borrowing for water main project
budget_items.what_was_said: Temporary borrowing comes due in August and the board weighed another four-month or six-month round; a decision awaits the contractor's schedule.
Expenditure details were received for a class action reimbursement; grant funding for testing is on standby.
Bid prices for treatment plants are rising sharply, so earlier projections are outdated.

budget_items.topic: Public criticism of project borrowing estimate
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident questioned the borrowing size against a smaller Ayer plant and the cost per household.

decisions.decision: Superintendent to calculate the bill at the first block rate, waive finance charges, and call the resident the next day.
Meter to be swapped for a new electronic meter and the old one tested off site.
Commissioners and superintendent to schedule a daytime walk of all Zone One areas.
Temporary borrowing decision deferred to the July 10th meeting after talking with the engineer.
Superintendent to send DEP guidance to the Planning Board and attend its July 8th meeting.

what_happened.line: Commissioners offered a resident a high-usage bill recalculated at the first block rate, finance charges waived, and a meter swap with the old meter tested off site.
The commissioners voted on updated rules and regulations; the recording does not make the outcome audible.
A decision on temporary borrowing for the Mass Ave water main project was deferred to the July 10th meeting, pending talks with the engineer.
The Hickory Hills security camera stayed in place after a privacy concern at the swim beach, and a daytime walk of Zone One was planned.
The superintendent is to send DEP guidance to the Planning Board and attend its July 8th meeting on the draft water protection bylaw.

why_it_matters: Water customers who see an unusually high quarterly bill have a route to a rate recalculation and a meter test, and the meter testing fee is not charged if the meter is found faulty.

The deferred borrowing and the draft water protection bylaw could affect water rates and what residents are later asked to approve, and rising PFAS treatment plant bid prices mean earlier cost projections are out of date.
